hook: The Dircks Residence of about 1875, home of the first boat builder at Hunters Point.

historical_record.description: Anderson & Cristofani bought the cottage and converted it into an office for their shipyard, which used it until 1997.
The Dircks Residence was built — one of three structures surviving from the earliest era of wooden boat building at India Basin.

Johnson J. Dircks, born in the Netherlands, was the first known boat builder to move to Hunters Point, establishing a yard at the corner of 5th (Evans) Avenue and L (Lane) Street. He moved all of his operations to a site next to William Stone's on 9th (Innes) Avenue in 1876.

historic_survey.finding: Appears eligible for the California Register under Criterion 1 (events) and Criterion 3 (design and construction) — a rare very early Italianate cottage, and one of only two nineteenth-century dwellings left in India Basin
historic_survey.physical_integrity: Retains location, design, setting, materials, workmanship, feeling and association
historic_survey.note: Recorded as the Dirks/Jorgenson Residence, common name the "Shipwrights' Cottage": a one-story-over-basement gable-roofed dwelling in rustic channel siding, its windows and door under bracketed hood mouldings, its raking cornice stripped of scroll-sawn trim not long before the survey. Vacant and in poor condition when recorded. The report spells the shipwright's name Dirks on this form and Dircks throughout its narrative. The district record leaves this property out of the proposed boat-yard district because its purpose was not maritime during the period of significance.
